questions.prompt: How does a child component send data up to its parent?

options.text: By emitting a custom event (declared with defineEmits) that the parent listens to with @event
By editing the parent's variables directly

questions.explanation: Children emit events; the parent listens with @eventName and updates its own state. Mutating props is not allowed (one-way data flow).

questions.prompt: What does a default v-model on a component desugar to?

options.text: A value prop and a change event
A modelValue prop and an update:modelValue event
A ref stored on the parent only

questions.explanation: By default, v-model on a component maps to a modelValue prop plus an update:modelValue event. defineModel wires this up automatically.

questions.prompt: Since which Vue version is the defineModel macro stable?
questions.explanation: defineModel became stable in Vue 3.4, simplifying two-way component bindings.

questions.prompt: The compile-time macro used to declare the events a component can emit is define______. (complete the word)
questions.explanation: defineEmits declares a component's events (with optional TypeScript payload types) and returns the emit function.

questions.prompt: How do you expose a named model for v-model:title on a child?
questions.explanation: const title = defineModel('title') creates a named model that the parent binds with v-model:title. A component can expose several named models.

questions.prompt: Match each mechanism to what it's for.

pairs.right: Pass data down to a child
Send events (data) up to the parent
The event a default v-model listens for

questions.explanation: Props go down, emits go up, defineModel creates two-way v-model, and update:modelValue is the event behind a default v-model.
